subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC follow-up — network / VPN / latency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC follow-up — network / VPN / latency targets

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment after the discovery:  

Summary of ACME targets (from call):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 100ms for interactive use (streaming enabled).
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions (typical session = streaming chat).
- Throughput: sustained ~500 requests/sec, spiky to ~800 rps with burst capacity.
- Streaming: client expects token-level updates with chunk latency <= 40ms once model starts streaming.

Private deployment notes we discussed:
- Deployment mode: Private VPC (Redwood private control plane, ACME-managed VPC peering or VPN).
- Network concerns: VPN vs. Direct Connect/Peering, egress IPs for allowlist, expected RTT budget between ACME app tier and Redwood inference nodes (~20–40ms allowed).

Next technical asks from our side (short term):
1) Can you share which AWS region and VPC (CIDR) you plan to peer/route to?
2) Will you use VPN (IPsec) or AWS Direct Connect/Transit Gateway? Any estimated baseline RTT to our target subnet?
3) Any firewall/NAT that will affect long-lived streaming TCP connections?
4) Can you provide a contact for CloudOps/SRE to exchange peering/firewall details (traceroute, allowed ports, sample payload size)?

I've attached the SLO requirements template we discussed and our network checklist. Rishi and Vivek (cc) will be your technical leads on the Redwood side; Jordan will handle contract/PO items.

Proposed next step: 30–45 min technical alignment call tomorrow 10:30–11:15 PT to review peering and run a short latency test plan. Does that work for you?

Thanks,
—Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-requirements.xlsx]

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acme.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC follow-up — network / VPN / latency targets

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the materials. Confirming numbers from our side and adding network details:  

Confirmed SLO targets:
- p95 end-to-end <= 100ms (target) — client is willing to accept p99 <= 250ms fallbacks during maintenance windows.
- Concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent streaming sessions; planning for 400 as an upper planning number.
- Throughput: baseline 500 rps sustained, peaks to 800–900 rps for short windows (60–120s).
- Streaming: we need token-chunk delivery with perceived inter-chunk latency <= 50ms on average; 40ms is ideal.

Network topology / constraints:
- Region: us-east-1 (N. Virginia).
- VPC CIDR: 10.32.0.0/16 (we can provide subnet-level details to your SREs).
- Connectivity: preference is to use AWS Transit Gateway + VPC peering to consolidate routes; we can stand up a VPN tunnel as fallback.
- Egress: our infra will NAT egress via shared NAT gateways; we can provide static egress IPs for allowlisting.
- Firewall: our perimeter allows long-lived TCP; internal ALBs terminate TLS and forward to app nodes — we do not currently proxy WebSocket-like persistent connections through a layer that would break streaming.

SRE contact: Tom Liu (cc) — Tom runs our CloudOps team and will coordinate network artifacts (traceroutes, VPC peering request, CIDRs). He can share a diagram and confirm expected intra-AZ RTT (our internal tests show 5–15ms within region; cross-subnet to a peer can be 15–35ms depending on path).

I'll ask Tom to send the peering diagram and a short list of firewall rules we can open for the pilot. We can also share a limited set of sample payloads for your latency testing.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of AI Platform
ACME Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC follow-up — network / VPN / latency targets

Hi Sarah — great, thanks for the detail. A few technical clarifications and what we'll do on our side:  

Quick clarifications:  
- When you say "token-chunk delivery" can you confirm average chunk size (tokens or bytes) for your typical streaming session? This affects our batching window.
- For concurrency, is 200 concurrent sessions measured as open streaming connections or active token throughput (i.e., many idle connections + bursts)?

What we need from ACME for a pilot (short list):
1) VPC peering/Transit Gateway request (CIDRs + peering owner account).
2) Traceroute/MTR from a representative app node to the target Redwood subnet (if you prefer, provide an ec2 we can ping from).
3) ACLs/firewall rules or list of NAT egress IPs to allowlist.
4) If using VPN/IPsec, a sample keepalive/DPD interval and expected tunnel RTT variance.

What we'll provide within 48 hours:
- redwood-network-checklist.pdf (attachment) — exact ports, TCP keepalive recommendations, recommended MTU, and preferred TLS settings for long-lived streaming.
- A runbook for a quick latency test (we'll provide a curl/stream script and expected metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99, per-token latency, handshake time).
- A short-scale performance run in our test environment to validate p95 numbers against an equivalent model and streaming setup.

If you can share the peering diagram and a contactable bastion or test host, we can set up a quick traceroute/iperf by end of week. Proposed tech sync: today 4:30 PT / tomorrow 10:30 PT — whichever works for Tom.

Attaching our network checklist now for reference.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-network-checklist.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Private VPC follow-up — network / VPN / latency targets

Thanks all — appreciated. Quick mutual action plan so nothing falls through:  

ACME (Tom/Sarah):
- Share VPC peering request + diagram (including CIDRs and peering owner account) — target: EOD 2026-03-23.
- Provide NAT egress IPs and any firewall ACLs that will be applied to Redwood traffic.
- Provide a sample app node (or allowlist a bastion) for traceroute/iperf testing.

Redwood (Rishi/Vivek):
- Provide checklist & runbook (done/attached) and a short stream test script — ETA 48 hours.
- Run initial latency/throughput test once traceroute host is available and share results (p50/p95/p99 and per-chunk latencies).
- Confirm required firewall ports and expected connection durations for pilot.

Commercial / Ops (Jordan/Marissa):
- Jordan to prepare draft SOW and PO template; Marissa to share pilot timeline and acceptance criteria (SLOs).
- If pilot looks good, Jordan will propose timeline and pricing for Dedicated private deployment.

I'll book the tech sync for tomorrow 10:30 PT and send a calendar invite. If that time doesn't work for Tom, please propose an alternate. Also attaching the Drive link where we'll track SLOs and test results.

Best,
—Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
